newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA may float major subsidiaries -paper.
newsitem.headline: SIA may float major subsidiaries -paper.

text.p: Singapore Airlines (SIA) might float major subsidiaries such as Singapore Airport Terminal Services, SIA Engineering and regional carrier SilkAir, the Business Times said on Tuesday.
It quoted SIA deputy chairman and chief executive officer Cheong Choong Kong as saying, when asked whether SIA plans to list the subsidiaries:

"I don't see why not, even though we've not given serious thought to it till now. We are not in need of funds, which removes a compelling reason for an IPO (initial public offer) but funding isn't the only reason for listing."

"There's a lot of value in each of those three companies that's not totally collected in SIA's consolidated balance sheet. A separate listing will realise that value for the SIA shareholder," Cheong said. He gave no timing indications.

He also said SIA's cargo division might be spun off as an independent subsidiary company within the next two to three years, and that short-haul tourist carrier SilkAir might be allotted long-haul routes suited to smaller aircraft.
He made the comments in an SIA in-house publication, the Business Times said.
